input.quote: The Agreement may be renewed for an additional period of seven (7) years at the option of the Licensor.
input.rationale: Article IV gives Licensor a unilateral option to extend the 36-month Initial Period by a further seven years, with no Licensee opt-out and no cap on renewal pricing. A multi-year renewal that the customer cannot decline is walk-away territory under the rule and fails the fallback (auto-renewal with a notice window of no more than 60 days and uplift ≤5%). The mutual-agreement language in sub-clauses II and III does not cure this, since the Licensor option sits in direct conflict with it. Redline moves to the preferred position: successive 12-month renewals, 30-day Licensee non-renewal notice, 60-day Licensor reminder and uplift capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%; a 60-day window with a 5% cap is an acceptable fallback.

proposal.summary: Replace Licensor's unilateral 7-year renewal option with 12-month renewals, 30-day Licensee opt-out and capped uplift
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We replaced the Licensor's unilateral seven-year renewal option with successive twelve-month renewals that we can decline on 30 days' notice, and capped any renewal uplift at the lesser of CPI and 3%. Our playbook does not permit automatic or unilateral multi-year renewals; a 60-day notice window and a 5% cap would be an acceptable fallback.

ops.oldText: The Agreement may be renewed for an additional period of seven (7) years at the option of the Licensor.
ops.newText: The Agreement may be renewed for successive additional periods of twelve (12) months each, unless Licensee gives written notice of non-renewal not less than thirty (30) days prior to the end of the then-current term. Licensor shall notify Licensee of any upcoming renewal not less than sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current term, and the fees for any renewal term shall not increase by more than the lesser of the increase in CPI and three percent (3%) over the fees for the immediately preceding term.
